title: Windows: the stored data is compressed on disk
changes: New in Settings → Stored data (Windows): Compress on disk, on to begin with. Windows keeps the stored data compressed on your drive, the same as ticking "Compress contents to save disk space" on the folder, so it takes roughly half the space. Nothing in it is removed and pages read it as normal.

Each time a save is loaded the new copy is compressed before it's used, which adds a little time to loading. Your current stored data is compressed the next time a save is loaded, or straight away if you switch the setting off and on.
Settings shows how much space the stored data takes on disk as well as its size. Works on NTFS drives (most Windows drives); elsewhere the file is left as it is.

title: Fix: prize money in Dynasty and Lifespans
changes: Fix: a person's prize money in the Dynasty members, totals and Lifespans was far too high. It added up the save's jockey, trainer, head trainer and manager totals, so a race you managed, trained and rode was counted up to three times, and the save's manager total runs well above what the stable actually won. It's now the race money of every race the person rode, trained or managed, each race counted once (the same way the wins next to it are counted).

title: Faster loading, and an option to compact the stored data
changes: Loading a save is faster: the sectional times already worked out are kept, and only new races are added, instead of working out every race's sectionals again each time. The results are exactly the same.

New in Settings: Stored data. Compact stored data (off to begin with) makes the stored copy smaller without losing anything you can see in the viewer. Each time a save is loaded it drops the game's rating history and race replays, its Yearly Summary story entries and their hidden data, and other people's horses' raw race positions once their sectional times are worked out (the sectionals are kept), and rebuilds the biggest tables without a duplicate copy of their ID index. What it drops can't come back.

Also thin other horses' charts (optional): other people's horses keep one stat and value point per quarter. Your stables' horses, horses you've ridden, bred or traded, their parents and your family are never thinned.
Compact now applies it straight away, and Settings shows how big the stored data is and what the last compacting saved.
Fix: Export CSV on the Horses list stopped with 'too many SQL variables' when the list held more than a few thousand horses. It now exports every horse.

title: Rebuild of 16.6
changes: A fresh build of 16.6 for Windows, Mac and Linux. Nothing in the viewer has changed.

title: Concepts and Qualifying under Racing; your own racing season
changes: New in Settings → Display: Racing season. Pick the day your season starts (1 August to start with; choose 1 January for calendar years). Jockey season, Concepts and their season pickers follow it, and seasons that cross the new year are labelled like 2018/19.

Also in Settings: Race series keep their own season. Turn it on and each series in Concepts runs from its first race to its last, whatever your season start, so a series that runs April to October isn't split.

New Racing → Concepts tab: every race series (Triple Crowns, Triple Tiaras, the Hong Kong series and more) with this season's races and winners, whether a horse is on for the sweep, and how often it has been swept. Seasons follow your racing season from Settings.
Click a series for every season side by side: who won each race (a horse that won more than one is highlighted), who swept it, and a 5–3–1 points table for any season.

New Racing → Qualifying tab: races you have to earn a place in, by points (the Kentucky Derby, Kentucky Oaks) or by finishing in the places in certain races (the Breeders' Cup races, Caulfield Cup, Cox Plate and more), with how many horses are in so far and how many are yours.
Click one for the standings this time round, where each horse earned its points or place, and every race that leads to it with its points or places and next date.
Both are also in the Racing side menu under Series & qualifying.

Fix: a person's Awards tab now includes stable awards (Stable of the Year, the Thravang Award and Breeder of the Year) for the stable's owner and everyone who managed it that year, with their role (Owner, Manager or both). They show in Latest awards and count in the Lifespans and Dynasty award totals too, and there's an As owner filter.

title: Training, syndicates, your season, compare, saved views and more
changes: New Training & plans tab on every horse: training programme, food and care with each one's effect on speed, stamina, strength and acceleration; shoes; yearly schedule; race plan; suggested campaigns; and the races it has qualified for.

Horse Overview: Rankings (career earnings, earnings for its age, offspring earnings and pedigree, as the game's top x%) and its Syndicate, with every shareholder. The Horse table has Earnings rank and Pedigree columns.
Stables: Facilities (what's built, cost to build, running costs a day) and Farm sponsors. Racecourses: their sponsors.
People: the languages they speak (on their page, as a column, and a Speaks… filter in People) and any syndicate shares they hold.

New Jockey season tab (and Your season on Home): this season against the same point last season, strike rate by course, distance and track, best partnerships with trainers, horses and stables, month by month, rides booked and ride offers.
New Compare: Compare… on any horse or person puts two side by side, with the better figure of each pair in green.
Saved views: ☆ Save this view on any list keeps your filters and sort under a name in your favourites, shown as chips above the list.
Home has a new For you panel: rides coming up, ride offers to answer, sponsor deals ending in the next 60 days, recent fan milestones and new qualifying runs.
The search box also finds horses by your notes and tags.
Settings → Tags: download a backup of your notes and tags, and bring one back (added to yours, or replacing them). Notes already there are never doubled up.
Sorting the Horse table by Fans or Sponsor no longer relies on SQLite working out a shortcut on its own: there's now a proper lookup for sponsors (plus ones for all the new data).

Fix: Horse finances counted auction sales twice. A horse sold at auction showed both Sale (the full price) and Sale (after auction house cut), on top of the Auction commission cost. Now it's just Sale at the full price with the commission as a cost, so the net is right; Sale (after auction house cut) is gone. Horses bought at auction were likewise counted twice as a Purchase and now count once. Older auctions the game kept no payment record for still count, the same way.

title: Whole group financials load quickly
changes: Whole group Financials and Horse finances are much faster: the group's payments are now looked up through the save's index instead of reading every payment in the game (over 1.7 million in a typical save). The group Financials tab went from about 1.5 seconds to a few hundredths of a second, and changing the year or month is just as quick.
Horse finances (one stable or the group) also find private horse sales faster.
Your own stable's Financials and Horse finances, for the stable and its whole group, are now got ready in the background when the viewer starts, so they open straight away.

title: Group financials for the stables a person owns
changes: New: Financials and Horse finances can show a whole ownership group. A group is every stable a person owns outright (all its shares) plus the stables those hold a majority of; for stables nobody owns outright, a parent stable and the stables it holds a majority of. Use the new This stable / Whole group switch at the top of either tab.
The group bar lists every stable in it and who holds it (e.g. Archer Bloodstock NZ, 100% held by Northwind Marine Archer Racing NZ).

Whole group Financials: income, expenses, net, cash and net worth added up month by month and year by year, with the same charts, year-by-year table and month-by-month breakdown. Payments between the group's stables are left out of the payment detail; in the monthly figures they show as income in one and spending in another, so the net is unaffected.

Whole group Horse finances: every horse the group has had, with its money in all the group's stables added up and the stables it was with under its name. Transfers between the group's stables drop out.
A person's page has a new Stables they own panel, with Group financials and Group horse finances buttons for each group they own.

title: Horse and concept awards for managers and staff
changes: A person's Awards tab now includes the horse and concept awards of horses they worked with: Horse of the Year, Champion Male, the age and sex champions, Hall of Fame nominations and concept awards such as Weight for Age Triple Crown (New Zealand) and Autumn Triple Crown (Japan). Each shows the horse and their role: Manager, Head trainer, Trainer, Jockey or Caretaker (or several, e.g. Manager & Trainer).

Managers share in every horse award and Group/Listed race win won while they managed the horse's stable. The game writes only one manager on each award, so before, a co-manager (or you) could miss out; this is the same fix 15.6 made for race wins.
Group 2, Group 3 and Listed wins on the Awards tab now count every role too (head trainer and manager, not just jockey).

New tiles on the person Awards tab: Own awards, Horse & concept awards, Group & Listed wins, and one for each role. The filter has Own awards, Horse awards, Race wins and As manager / trainer / jockey… options.
These awards also appear in the person's Latest awards (with the horse and role) and count in the award totals on the Lifespans, Dynasty and family pages.

title: Softer family tree highlights in dark mode
changes: Dark mode: ancestors you highlight in a family tree (8 to 16 generations) are now a soft tint of their colour with the name in that colour, instead of a solid bright block. The same goes for the highlight key above the tree and the “highlighted” count beside each generation. Light mode is unchanged.

title: Your stables stand out in every table
changes: The gold highlight from Top sires and dams is now in every table that isn't about stables: rows for horses (and people) in stables you own are gold with a bar down the left, and a small key under the table explains it. That includes All horses, the Horse table, race results and entries, people and jockey lists, the home page, and the race records and offspring on horse and person pages.
Stables you own include ones your stables own; ones you only manage or hold shares in aren't highlighted. A race result shows the stable each horse ran for that day.

The stable pages and stable lists (All stables, Stable table, Rankings) aren't highlighted, and nor is a table where every row is yours (your own horse's race record, say), since there'd be nothing to pick out.

title: Your sires and dams stand out
changes: Top sires, Top dams and Broodmare sires: rows for horses in stables you own are highlighted (gold, with a bar down the left) and marked Yours in the Stable column. Stables you own include ones your stables own; ones you only manage or hold shares in aren't highlighted.
A new stable filter there shows Your stables only (also in the CSV export).

title: Tags in Settings and a log of notes on horses
changes: Tags are now made in Settings → Tags (also in the Settings side menu): type a name, pick one of ten colours and click Create tag (or press Enter). Rename, recolour and delete them on the same page; deleting a tag takes it off every horse (it asks first).
On a horse's Fans, sponsors & notes tab you just tick your tags: Your tags lists them all, and clicking one puts it on that horse or takes it off. It shows beside the horse's name straight away.

Notes are now a log. Your notes sits on the right of the tab: write a note and press Enter to save it (Shift+Enter starts a new line). Each note shows when you wrote it and the game date at the time, newest first.
Edit or delete any note: Edit opens it in place (Enter saves, Esc cancels) and Delete asks once before it goes. When there are more notes than fit, the list scrolls inside its box.
Your existing note on each horse is kept as the first entry in its log.
Horses → Notes & tags shows each horse's tags, latest note and how many notes it has, and searches every note. Your tags are listed at the top with how many horses have each.

title: Fans, sponsors and notes on horses
changes: New tab on every horse's page: Fans, sponsors & notes. Tiles show its fans, its world rank by fans among living horses, its fan level, its sponsor now and everything its sponsors have paid (and any merchandise offers for your horses).

Fan milestones: the save keeps the best world fan ranking each horse has reached, so every horse now shows how far it has climbed: Fan website (top 100 by fans), Supporters' club (top 50), Fan club trips (top 20), Superfans (top 10) and No. 1. For your own horses each step has the date from your inbox. A step it has since dropped out of is marked Not any more, with its rank now.

Sponsors: every sponsor the horse has had, with the industry, monthly payment, win bonus, contract dates, wins during the contract and total paid. From your inbox (your horses): the website, supporters' club, fan club trip, superfan and merchandise messages about it, with the fans and rank at the time and the money offered or asked for.

New: your own notes and tags on any horse, in Your notes & tags on that tab. Click a tag to tick or untick it (Website, Fan club and Merchandise to start). To make your own, type a name in New tag, pick one of ten colours and click Add tag: it's ticked on that horse straight away and shows beside its name. Write anything in the notes box: it saves as you type. Your tags show beside the horse's name on every tab of its page and in the horse lists, together with the automatic tags, and a note icon you can point at reads your note.

Automatic tags in All horses and the Horse table: outlined chips for each horse's fan level (dashed, with its rank now, if it has since dropped out of that level, e.g. “No. 1 by fans · now #2”), Sponsored if it has a sponsor now, and Merch if you've been offered a merchandise deal for it. The tag filter has them (Auto: …) alongside your own tags, Tagged by you and With your notes.
Horse table: new Fans, Fan level (with its rank now if it isn't at that level any more) and Sponsor columns. Sort by fans or by monthly sponsorship; they're in the CSV export too.

New Horses → Notes & tags page (also in the Horses side menu): every horse you've tagged or written about, newest change first, with a search across names and notes. Rename, recolour (ten colours), add and delete tags there; deleting a tag takes it off every horse (it asks first).

Only you see your notes and tags. They're kept with the database (next to its data, not in the game), so they stay when you load a newer save into it, and move with it when an old-layout database is converted.

title: Manager wins shared fairly between co-managers
changes: Fixed: a stable with two managers split its wins between them, because the game writes only one manager on each race result. A manager could have fewer wins than the races they trained at their own stable. Now a stable's race counts for every manager it had that day (from each manager's start and end dates there), so co-managers share the same wins, places, prize money and Group and Listed wins.

This applies everywhere managers are counted: the Managers table on the People overview (any year, working now or everyone), the As a manager section on a person's Overview (with its latest races and Group & Listed wins), and the Dynasty and Lifespans pages. Races from before anyone's job records were kept still go to the manager the game wrote down.

Dynasty pages now count wins in every role from the race results, the same way as the People overview: Jockey wins, Trainer wins and a new Manager wins column in the Members table and the totals. A person's wins on the cards (Pride of the family, the family tree, Lifespans) are the different races they won as a jockey, trainer or manager, each race once; point at the number to see the split.
The Managers table and the As a manager section say how manager wins are counted. Jockey stats' As manager prize money is the game's own figure, and now says so when you point at it.

title: Lifespans tab and a new Dynasty tab
changes: New Lifespans tab on every person, next to Tree chart: the person and their ancestors on one time line. Each life is a bar and the darker part is their racing career (point at it for the job, stable and years). Dots mark season awards, their first win, their first Group 1, marriages and children, and a dashed line shows the game date.

Lifespans lets you choose how far back to go (parents, grandparents, great-grandparents or everyone) and add brothers and sisters, children or both. Underneath: the average age at a first child, the youngest first win, the longest career, how long the person and their oldest ancestor overlapped, the jobs in the family, and the wins, Group 1s and awards between them.
The Dynasty tab now has three views: Overview, Family tree and Chronicle.

Overview: the family's crest and founders, the head of the family (the eldest living member of the earliest generation), totals for jockey and trainer wins, Group 1s, season awards, prize money and stables, the most decorated members, the family's stables (with their wins, Group 1s and horses) and the other stables where family members work, every generation, and the members table, which now also has Group 1s, awards and prize money.

Family tree: drawn from the founders down, with partners beside each member (a dashed line for a divorce), crowns for the head of the family, and buttons to highlight jockeys, trainers, award and Group 1 winners or who's working now. Zoom with − Fit +, drag to move around, and click a name to see the tree from them. Outline gives the old list for big families. Branches sums up each of the founders' children's lines.

Chronicle: the family's story decade by decade (births, marriages, divorces, deaths, stables founded, first wins, first Group 1s with the horse and race, and season awards), newest or oldest first, family or racing only. Beside it: living family members year by year, wins per decade and milestones.
Season awards on the dynasty pages now count wins only (runners-up and Hall of Fame nominations aren't counted).
Yearly charts with many years show fewer year labels so they don't overlap.

title: A clearer yearly income chart
changes: Fixed: the Income vs expenses by year chart on a stable's Financials tab now reads as a yearly chart. Its axis shows one year under each dot, with no months or dates such as "2 Jul 2017" along the bottom.
Pointing at the chart shows the year ("2019") instead of a date, and no longer repeats the year under Income.

A year with fewer than 12 months on record (the year in progress, or the first year of a stable) has a hollow dot, a faint dotted line to it and "10 mo" under the year, so a few months don't look like a sudden fall or rise. Pointing at it says "10 of 12 months so far".
The figures under the chart now say which year they're for, for example "2020 (2 of 12 months)", and use short amounts so they fit on one line. Net has dots too.
The chart's CSV download has a Year column instead of a date.
Fixed: leaving the Settings page before it had finished loading could log an error.

title: Breeding income by horse
changes: New: on a stable's Financials tab, the Income detail now breaks breeding fees down by horse. Open Breeding fees → Transfer with ▸ and each of your stallions gets its own row: how many covers it was paid for, its total, its average fee and its share, biggest earner first. Compare what each horse earns at stud for a whole year or a single month.
▸ on a horse lists its covers (date, who paid, which mare, amount). By horse · Each payment switches back to the plain list of every payment.

The horse is worked out from the game's note on each payment ("Breeding fee for <mare> and <stallion>"): the one your stable owns, or otherwise the stallion. A horse you've since sold says where it is now, and a mare is marked as such (for example a refund for a breeding failure).
The payment search box finds horses by name too: type one and only that horse's row is left.

title: Favourites and shortcut keys
changes: New: favourites. Every page has a star (☆) in the menu bar, next to refresh. Click it to add the page you're on to a new Favourites list at the top of the side menu; the star turns gold while the page is a favourite, and clicking it again takes it off. Any page can be a favourite: a horse, a person, a stable's financials, a race, a filtered list such as Trainers or Group 1 results.

Favourites get the page's name (for example "Northwind Marine Archer Racing NZ · Financials"). To rename one, click Rename on the message that appears, or point at it in the side menu and click ✎. ✕ removes it (with Undo), and you can drag favourites up and down to change the order.
Favourites belong to the database that's open, because a horse or stable number means something different in another save. With the side menu shrunk to icons they show as icons.

New: shortcut keys, on a new Settings → Shortcuts tab. It lists every page in the side menus, the You pages (your profile, stable, horses and stable's races), your favourites and the menu-bar buttons (back, forward, refresh, add to favourites, search, side menu, light/dark, load new database). None have a key to start with.

To set one, click Set a key and press the keys you want, such as Ctrl + Shift + H, Alt + 1, F2 or a single letter. Keys already used by the viewer, Windows, the Mac or the browser (copy, paste, undo, F5, zoom, Alt + arrows…) are refused with the reason. If the key is already on another page it moves to the new one and says so. ✕ or Backspace removes a key, Esc stops without changing anything, and Remove all shortcuts clears them all. A search box finds pages quickly.

Shortcuts don't fire while you're typing in a box, unless they use Ctrl, Alt or Cmd, and they wait while a window such as Load new database is open. The favourites star shows its key when you point at it.
Settings → Reset settings leaves your favourites and shortcuts alone.

title: HRM Viewer for Mac
changes: New: HRM Viewer for Mac. Download HRM-Viewer-15.1-mac.zip from the releases page (about 30 MB). One download works on every Mac with macOS 11 Big Sur or later, Apple Silicon (M1 and later) and Intel alike.
Installing: double-click the zip to unzip it, then drag HRM Viewer into your Applications folder and open it.

The first time you open it, the Mac says it "could not verify" HRM Viewer, because the app isn't signed with a paid Apple developer account (it's signed for free instead). Click Done, open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway next to HRM Viewer, then confirm. This is only needed once; after that it opens like any other app.

Size: the app is bigger once unzipped than the download, because it carries its own Python for both kinds of Mac (Apple Silicon and Intel), so there's nothing else to install and one download fits every Mac. The first time it opens, it copies the viewer and the Python your Mac uses into your Library/Application Support/HRM Viewer folder; that copy is what runs.

Your data: databases and settings are kept in Library/Application Support/HRM Viewer in your home folder, not inside the app, so they stay when you replace the app with a newer download, and updates installed from inside the viewer stay too (opening the app doesn't put its own older version back).

It opens in its own window with the usual Mac menus: Edit (copy, paste, select all, undo), Window (minimise, zoom, close) and Quit (Cmd+Q). Quitting, closing the window, or Quit from the Dock all stop the viewer properly.

Updates work like on Windows: the viewer offers new versions by itself, and Settings → Install an update takes an update file. Going back to an earlier version is offered back to 14.6, the first version made for Mac and Linux.
Files you download in the viewer (CSV, chart pictures, the Quick Guide) are saved to your Downloads folder, with a Show in Finder button; links to websites open in your browser.

Tested before release on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 15: opening, the copy to Application Support, downloads, an update from inside the viewer, reopening, quitting, and the Mac's check of a downloaded copy (it asks for Open Anyway, it doesn't call the app damaged). Loading a save and the Open Anyway click itself haven't been tried on a real Mac yet, so please say if anything doesn't work.

title: Linux: opens in its own window on more systems
changes: Linux: HRM Viewer now works with WebKitGTK 4.0 as well as 4.1. Many systems (Ubuntu 22.04, Linux Mint and others) come with 4.0, which before made it open in the browser.

Linux: if the window can't start because of the graphics driver (a blank or crashing window, common with some NVIDIA cards and virtual machines), it tries again with WebKitGTK's safe graphics settings, and remembers what worked for next time.
Linux: when it still has to open in the browser, Settings now says why (for example "WebKitGTK 4.1 isn't installed"), and so does data/desktop.log.

title: The same filters on every table
changes: Every table's filters now look and work the same, in the same order: what the table lists (Sires · Dams, Jockeys · Trainers, Expenses · Income…), the search box, the status, dropdowns, then from–to ranges (Age, Foals foaled).

Status is always Alive · Deceased · All for horses and people, and Active · Closed · All for stables. People, Jockeys & trainers, Pedigrees, Family and Dynasty can now show just the deceased, and Stables and the Stable table just the closed ones.
Dropdowns with no filter always say Any … (Any sex, Any type, Any country, Any class…), and year menus say All years.
Search boxes always say what they search: Search horses, Search races, Search stables, Search people, Search payments, Search this table…
New Clear filters button at the end of a filter bar whenever a filter is set: puts them all back to how they start (keeping what the table lists).
All filter controls are the same height and style, including the year and month menus on Financials; the selected option shows clearly in dark mode.
Lists say 1 stable, 1 person and so on, instead of 1 stables.

title: Expense and income detail: any year, any month
changes: Stable Financials: the Expense / Income detail now has a year menu with every year on record, and a month menu (Whole year, or any month in that year).
Years and months in the game's payment log show every payment, grouped by category and type, as before, now for a single month too.

Earlier years and months (the game keeps only a yearly total of older payments) show the breakdown by category from the monthly figures, with the total, a monthly average and each category's share. The month menu marks which months come from the monthly figures.
When a year's payment log is incomplete (for example it only starts in October), the detail says so.

title: Fix: Linux app when it can't open a window
changes: Linux: if HRM Viewer can't open its own window (for example the screen isn't reachable, or the window part fails to start), it now opens in your browser instead of closing straight away.

title: HRM Viewer for Linux (Mac coming soon)
changes: New: HRM Viewer for Linux and Steam Deck desktop mode. Download HRM-Viewer-<version>-linux.tar.gz, unpack it and open HRM Viewer. It opens in its own window when WebKitGTK is installed, otherwise in your browser, and offers to add itself to your applications menu.
It comes with its own Python, so there's nothing to install, and it takes updates from inside the viewer just like the Windows app.
In the Linux window, downloads (CSV, chart pictures, the Quick Guide) are saved to your Downloads folder with a Show in folder button, and outside links open in your browser.
A Mac version (Apple Silicon and Intel) is built and being tested; it will follow in a later update.
The viewer now stops by itself if its window closes unexpectedly, instead of staying running in the background.
Security: the viewer now refuses requests to change things that come from other websites open in your browser.
The "type a path" boxes show an example path for your system (Windows or Linux).

title: Stable rankings
changes: New Rankings tab under Stables: league tables of every open stable, like the game's own. Choose Cash earnings, Times, Staff, Prestige, Horses, Traders, Breeders or Value.
Each table shows the rank, stable, owner and country (with its flag), and your stables are highlighted. Your stables shows just yours with their rank, and search finds a stable, owner or country.
Cash earnings, Times and Traders can be seen for any year or all time. Prestige shows how many places each stable has moved since 1 January.
Value uses the stable's market value with its horses, property (racecourses and auction houses), cash, loans and net worth.
Country flags now show on Windows too, using a small bundled flag font (Twemoji, CC BY 4.0).

title: Fix: People page error on Windows
changes: Fixed the People page showing "[Errno 22] Invalid argument" on Windows in 14.3. Windows can't convert dates before 1970 the way 14.3 did, and saves have races going back to the 1800s. Dates are now worked out in a way that works for any year.
The same fix for the Horse finances tab, which could hit the same error for very old records.

title: Faster pages, clearer tables and charts
changes: People overview opens faster (about 6 seconds down to 4 the first time after loading a save, and it's done in the background), and switching to another year now takes a fraction of a second instead of about 4 seconds.
Horse finances tab opens faster: horse names for trading fees are matched once per save instead of every time.
Charts: money charts now pick Linear or Log for you. Log is used only when a few values dwarf the rest, so the year-by-year chart and Net worth & cash read naturally (Linear / Log still switches).
Charts: new Smooth button on charts with lots of points, which averages each point with its neighbours to show the trend through the monthly ups and downs.
Charts: lines are brighter in dark mode so they stand out, and they recolour straight away when you switch modes.
Charts: time ranges too short to show anything (such as 1M on a monthly chart) are no longer offered, so the buttons fit on one row.
Tables: a faint ↕ shows on a heading you can sort by; headings can be sorted from the keyboard (Tab, then Enter).
Tables: clicking a group heading above the columns (such as Group & Listed) no longer sorts the table by the wrong column.
Behind the scenes: removed unused code and styles and shared a few repeated pieces.

title: People overview by year, and everyone
changes: People overview: pick a year at the top to see jockeys, trainers and managers for that season (races, wins, prize money, Group and Listed wins in that year), or All time.
Choose Working now or Everyone (incl. retired) to include people who have retired, died or are out of work.
Each table now has a rank column and a Show all link that lists every jockey, trainer or manager, 25 per page; Top 8 only goes back.

title: Tidier People overview
changes: People overview: the Group & Listed wins list under the Jockeys, Trainers and Managers tables is gone; each person's Group, Listed and combined wins are already in the table.

title: New Overview for each person
changes: A person's Overview tab now has a section for each role: As a jockey, As a trainer and As a manager, all laid out the same way.

Each shows their current job and stable in that role, their races, wins and strike rate, places, prize money, Group wins (with the G1/G2/G3 split), Listed wins and the two together; their latest races (Show all for up to 50); and their Group & Listed wins with a switch between All, Group and Listed.
Roles someone has never had show a short line instead of an empty section.

Latest awards and Latest news are now small panels beside the roles, newest first, opening with Show more. The tiles at the top show their job now, Group and Listed wins in any role, awards, reputation and fame.
Quick Guide updated.

title: People overview
changes: Clicking People now opens an overview page (All people is still in the side menu).

Three sections, Jockeys, Trainers and Managers, laid out the same way: the top 8 working now with their stable, age, races, wins and strike rate, prize money, Group wins (with the G1/G2/G3 split), Listed wins, the two together, and their latest race. Under each, the section's latest Group and Listed wins with Group, Listed and Total counts.
Beside them, compact Latest awards and Latest news panels (newest first). They show a few items and open with Show more.
Quick Guide updated.

title: Tree chart; divorces on the Dynasty tab
changes: New Tree chart tab on people's pages: the family drawn as a proper tree with connecting lines. Ancestors above (up to 8 generations), the person in the middle with brothers and sisters beside them and partners next to them, children and grandchildren below. Zoom in and out, Fit, drag to move around, and click any name to put them in the centre.
Former partners stand on the person's left with a dashed line; the current partner on the right with a solid one.

Dynasty tab: people who married into the family and later divorced are now listed as Divorced (with their own filter and a Divorced tag), not as married in. Married to shows “divorced <year>”, and the family tree greys out former partners.
Quick Guide updated.

title: Family tree and Dynasty tabs for people
changes: People's pages have a new Family tree tab: ancestors up to 8 generations back (four as a chart, all eight in a fold-out list that says who each one is, e.g. “Father's mother's father”), and every relative the save links to them, named precisely (half-sister, great-uncle, first cousin once removed...). Switch between Close family, + Aunts, uncles & cousins, and Everyone, or show only those alive.

New <surname> dynasty tab: the family that shares the person's last name, from its earliest known member down. Tree by generation with who each married, every member and those who married in, stables owned, total jockey and trainer wins and awards, and a list of births, marriages, divorces and deaths.
The game links parents and children born since your career began, so family trees and dynasties grow as generations pass.
Quick Guide updated.

title: Horse finances: what each horse cost to buy
changes: Horse finances now counts private horse sales, not just auctions: what the stable paid to buy a horse shows as Purchase, and what it got for selling one as Sale.

If one of the stable's group stables (its parent stable, sub-stables or their sister stables) bought a horse and then passed it on to this stable, that price shows here too, as Purchase by <that stable>. Any fee paid between the group's own stables shows as Transfer fee within the group.
Horses bought privately are now listed from the day they were bought, so their costs and income are counted from then.

title: Awards tabs for horses and people; month by month
changes: Horse pages and people's pages now have an Awards tab, like stables. A horse's lists every season award and Group/Listed race win, with the jockey and stable. A person's lists their own awards plus every Group/Listed race win they rode, trained, managed or looked after, with a filter for each role. Filter by kind, wins only, year, or search.
Stable Financials: new Month by month panel with each month's income, expenses and net for the year you pick; ▸ opens that month's categories.
Stable Financials: the payment detail has an Expenses · Income switch, so you can see every payment the stable received, grouped the same way, with who paid (people, stables and racecourses by name).
Stable Overview: the Latest month panel is gone (the figures are on Financials, month by month).
The CSV button on tables that show one year at a time exports the year you're looking at.
Quick Guide updated for all of this.

title: Stable awards: Worst Horse of the Year
changes: On a stable's Awards tab, Worst Horse of the Year is now shown as “Worst of the year” instead of a win: it isn't highlighted, isn't counted in the “won” totals and doesn't appear under Wins only.
The Quick Guide now covers the stable Awards tab added in 13.3.

title: Awards tab on the stable page
changes: New Awards tab on every stable's page, next to Horse finances. It lists every award tied to the stable: the stable's own awards (Stable of the Year, Thravang, Breeder of the Year, Hall of Fame and race-series awards), every award its horses won while they were in the stable (season awards and Group and Listed race wins), and every award its employees won while they worked there.
Filter by Stable, Horse awards, Race wins or Employees, show wins only, pick a year, or search by name. The filters are kept in the page address, so refreshing keeps them.
A horse or employee who moves on later keeps the award with the stable they won it for.

title: Refresh button; dark mode table headings
changes: New ↻ Refresh button next to back and forward: it loads the page you're on again with the latest data and keeps your place. F5 does the same.
Dark mode: the first heading of wide tables (such as Award on the Awards pages) no longer shows up highlighted in a brown colour. All table headings now use the same colour.

title: Never stuck on a busy port
changes: The viewer now finds its own free port. If the usual one (8765) is taken, it tries the next 500, and if every one of those is taken it asks Windows for any free port, so it always opens.
It skips straight past ports Windows keeps for itself (Hyper-V, WSL, Docker), and waits a moment for a port that's only just been let go of.
HRM Viewer.exe follows whichever port the viewer opened, and uses the same one next time so your display settings stay put. A restart after an update keeps the same port too.

title: Each database follows its player
changes: Each database now keeps track of its player. If you load a save whose player is different (for example your heir has taken over) the viewer asks first: is it the same world? Same world keeps using this database for the new player; New player creates a separate database for them.
A save from a different world gets the same question, with loading it as a new database recommended.
Automatic updates ask too: when the watched save changes player or world, the question pops up instead of the save being loaded or quietly skipped.
Settings → Databases shows each database's player and any players it followed before, and its buttons are smaller.
Settings → Viewer → Updates has a new Check for updates automatically switch. Untick it and the viewer never looks for new versions by itself; Check now still works.

title: Clearer message when the port is taken
changes: If another program grabs the viewer's address just as it starts, HRM Viewer.exe now says so straight away (close that program or restart your PC) instead of a general “stopped while starting”.
The viewer tells apart “HRM Viewer is already running” from “another program has the port”, and a port clash never undoes an update you've just installed.

title: Fix: stuck on “Almost there…”
changes: If another program on the computer was already using the viewer's usual address (port 8765), HRM Viewer.exe waited forever on “Almost there…”. It now notices and uses the next free port instead, so the window opens.
On Windows the viewer now takes its port to itself, so it can't end up sharing one with another program.
If you were stuck, update by downloading HRM-Viewer-12.8-full.zip from the download page and copying your old data folder into it (or close the other program and open HRM Viewer again).

title: New home on GitHub
changes: HRM Viewer now lives at github.com/HRMViewer/hrm-viewer. Updates, All versions and the download page all use the new address (the old one still forwards there).

title: Stables you manage, and Jockey stats
changes: Your stables now includes the stables you manage, listed first and marked Manager (or Owner & manager). The side menu, the ◀ ▶ bar on stable pages and Settings → Main stable all follow.
Stable pages show the stable's manager next to its owner.

New People → Jockey stats page: every person's jockey, trainer and stable numbers side by side. Rides, wins, strike rate and prize money as a jockey and as a trainer (head trainer races included), the stable they work at now with its wins and prize money, how many stables they've managed and what they've earned as a manager.
Switch between Jockeys, Trainers, Stable managers and Everyone, search by name, filter by the job they do now, and sort by any heading. Your own row is highlighted.

title: All, alive or deceased on the home page
changes: Every horse table on the home page has All, Alive and Deceased buttons: your stable's horses, Top earners, Highest rated, Most wins, Top earners of all time, Most Group 1 wins and Leading sires.
Each table remembers its own choice. They start as before: your horses, Top earners and Highest rated show horses that are alive; the all-time boards show every horse.
Horses that have died are marked Dead, and their age is the age they reached.

title: Just download and open
changes: The full download now has everything it needs, including its own Python: unzip it and double-click HRM Viewer.exe. Nothing else to install.
HRM Viewer.exe is the only way to open the viewer now, in its own window. Start.bat and Load database.bat are gone (old copies are tidied away); drag a database.db onto HRM Viewer.exe to load it.
When a new version is out, the viewer asks when it opens: Install now, Remind me later or Skip this version, with what's new in it.

Settings → Viewer → Updates always uses the HRM Viewer repository on GitHub. All versions lists every published version, so you can go back to an earlier one if you don't like a new one, or update again.

title: Connected to GitHub
changes: The viewer now gets its updates from github.com/jomdesa-glitch/hrm-viewer by itself: when a new version is published there, the bar at the top offers to install it. Nothing to set up.
Anyone can download the full viewer from the Releases page of that repository.
Settings → Viewer → Updates from GitHub shows the repository and has Check now.

title: Updates from GitHub
changes: The viewer can now get new versions from GitHub. When a newer version is published, a bar at the top says so, with Install now, What's new and Later.

Install now downloads the update from GitHub and installs it the same way as Install an update: your data isn't touched, the viewer restarts on the new version, and Versions & changes can put the old one back.
Settings → Viewer has a new Updates from GitHub row: whether you're up to date, Check now, and a link to the download page where anyone can get the full viewer.
The viewer checks when it opens and every 6 hours while it's open. Install an update (choosing a zip by hand) still works as before.

title: Choose how the banner looks
changes: Once a photo is the banner, the gallery shows Banner view: a live preview of the hover card's banner and controls for how it looks.

Drag the preview to pick which part of the picture shows, zoom in (up to 400%), choose Fill the banner or Whole picture (with a background colour), pick Short, Medium or Tall, and Sharp pixels for pixel-art pictures.
Changes save by themselves and show on the horse's hover card straight away. Reset view puts it back; choosing a different banner starts with the standard view.

title: Hover-card banner only when you choose one
changes: A horse's hover card only shows a picture when you've picked one with ▭ Banner in its gallery. If no banner is chosen, the hover card has no picture, even if the horse has photos (it no longer falls back to the profile photo).

title: Tidier Settings, and a cleaner Quick Guide PDF
changes: Settings: Your stables is now a small panel at the top right, with Viewer and Database stacked underneath it, next to Display. Automatic updates stays full width below.
Quick Guide PDF: every section now stays whole on one page — no boxes split between pages.

title: Gallery: banners, and a sliding row of photos
changes: Each photo in a horse's gallery now has two choices: ★ Profile (next to the horse's name, and small in the horse lists) and ▭ Banner (across the top of the horse's hover card). Without a banner, the hover card uses the profile photo as before.
The gallery shows your photos in one row that slides sideways — use ‹ › or scroll — instead of wrapping onto new rows, with the number of photos above it. There's no limit on how many you add.
Delete is now a small ✕ on each photo (click twice).

title: Updates and the guide live in Settings
changes: “Install an update” is no longer at the bottom of every page — it's in Settings (and Settings → Versions & changes).
Settings has a new Quick Guide row: “Open the guide” shows the PDF inside the viewer, and “Download PDF” saves a copy. The guide is updated with every version.

title: Horse photo as a profile picture
changes: A horse's main photo is now a profile picture beside its name (a rounded square, a bit bigger than the small ones in lists) instead of a wide banner across the top of the page. Click it to open the gallery.

title: Horse photo gallery, and steadier gear tooltips
changes: Horse pages have a photo gallery: click “Add photos” (or “Gallery”) to upload pictures — click to choose or drag them in (JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP, up to 25 MB each).

Choose a main photo with “★ Use as main photo”. It shows across the top of the horse's page (click it to open the gallery), and small next to the horse's name in All horses, the Horse table and on its hover card.
Click a photo in the gallery to see it full size; delete any you don't want (click Delete twice). Photos are kept with each database, on your computer.
Gear letters: the mouse pointer no longer turns into a question mark, and the full gear names stay put while you move across the letters instead of jumping and restarting.

title: Quick Guide as a PDF, kept up to date
changes: The Quick Guide is now a PDF (“HRM Viewer - Quick Guide.pdf” next to HRM Viewer.exe), with the version and date on the front and page numbers.

It now comes with every update, not just the full download, and is refreshed for each new version. Installing an update puts the newest guide in your HRM Viewer folder (replacing the older HTML guide).

title: Choose your own colours
changes: Settings → Colours (under Appearance): pick your own colours for the accent (buttons, links, selected tabs), top bar, headings, page background, cards, lines and winning rows.
One-click presets: Racing green, Royal purple, Crimson, Ocean, Warm and a light top bar (and Black for dark mode).
Light and dark mode each keep their own colours — switch mode to change the other set. Changes show straight away; ✕ puts one colour back, or reset them all.
A light top bar automatically gets dark text so it stays readable.

title: Back and forward buttons
changes: New ‹ and › buttons at the top left (next to ☰) take you back and forward through the pages you've visited, like a web browser. They're greyed out when there's nowhere to go.
Alt + ← / Alt + → and your mouse's back / forward buttons do the same.

title: No more green boxes in Last starts
changes: Last starts (in a runner's form): removed the green boxes that appeared around some Track, Distance, Jockey and Cond. cells. They were an unexplained “same as this race” marker; the table is now clean. Winning runs keep their light green row.

title: Every table and chart: tidier and more useful
changes: Charts: every chart now has a tool row — Linear / Log switch (for any chart with amounts; positions stay as they are), the time range, ⤢ to open it large, PNG to save a picture, and CSV to download the numbers behind it.
Charts: gridlines fall on round numbers ($75M, $100M, $125M… instead of $112.52M), a log-scale chart says so on the picture, and narrow ranges on a log scale still get useful gridlines.

Charts: the legend shows each line's latest value; double-click a name to show only that line (double-click again for all). Single-line charts show Latest, High and Low (with dates) and the change over the range in view.
Tables with 25 or more rows get a Filter rows box next to their CSV button (shows “22 of 152”; Esc clears it) — fold-out rows stay with their row.
Long tables (over 30 rows) scroll inside themselves with the column headings, and any totals row, kept in view.
Every column heading that can sort now shows ⇅ when you point at it.

title: Horse finances tab for every stable
changes: New Horse finances tab on every stable page (next to Overview and Financials): money in and out for every horse the stable has had, now and in the past.
At the top: how many horses, what they earned, what was spent on them, the net and return, and the most profitable and costliest horse.

Income from horses and Spending on horses: what the money is made of across all the horses (prize money, sales, stud fees, sponsorship; purchases, feed & care, training, entry fees, travel, vet, win shares and so on).

Every horse: status (in the stable, sold, died, left, and where it is now), when it was with the stable, starts and wins, income, expenses, net and return. Show all / in the stable / past, find a horse, sort any column, download as CSV, and open any horse for its full breakdown and year-by-year figures.
Only money while the horse was with this stable is counted. Costs that aren't tied to one horse (facilities, wages, subscriptions) aren't included.
A few new lookups are built once, in a few seconds, the first time 10.5 starts.

title: Nicer, more useful Financials tables
changes: Income by category and Expenses by category: biggest categories first, short amounts (exact on hover), each row shaded so you can spot that category's big years, a little trend line, the change on the year before as a ▲▼ badge, and a bar for each category's share of the latest year.
New “% of year” switch shows every category as a share of that year's total.
A year still in progress is compared with the same months of the year before, in these tables as well.
Sorting by a column uses the exact amounts, and the CSV download has exact amounts too.

Expense detail: a summary strip (paid out, number of payments, biggest category), a filter box (type, note or who was paid), Open all / Close all, categories you can fold away, an Average column and share bars. Long lists start with only the biggest category opened out.

title: Nicer Year by year table
changes: Stable Financials → Year by year is easier to read: big year labels, short amounts ($58.35M), with the exact figure when you hover.
Changes on the year before are small green/red ▲▼ badges under each amount (for expenses, going up is red). Hover a badge for the exact comparison.
A year still in progress (e.g. “10 mo”) is now compared with the same months of the year before, instead of the whole previous year, so the change is fair.
Net shows the profit margin underneath, and the latest year is highlighted.

title: Stable Financials tab
changes: Stable pages now have two tabs: Overview and Financials. The ◀ ▶ stable switcher keeps you on the tab you're on.
Financials shows income and expenses year by year (with the change on the year before and the net result), plus each year by category using the game's own income and expense categories.

Under that, Expense detail breaks one year's payments down by category, then by type, and you can open any type to see each individual payment (date, who was paid, note, amount). This comes from the game's payment log, which only keeps recent years in detail.
The Net worth & cash and Income vs expenses charts moved from Overview to Financials, with the same figures. The Latest month summary stays on Overview.

The stable charts now use a logarithmic scale (marked “Log scale”), so one huge month no longer flattens everything else. $0 and negative amounts (like a negative net worth) still show; hovering still gives the exact amounts.
A new lookup on the payment log is built once, in a second or two, the first time 10.2 starts.

title: Tidier CSV export buttons
changes: List pages (Horses, Races, Meetings, the horse and stable tables and so on) now have just one export button: Export CSV at the top, which downloads every matching row. The second small “CSV (this page)” box is gone.
Every other table has one neat “⤓ CSV” button, placed on the table's own heading line (next to the panel title or sub-heading) instead of in a separate box above the table.
Export buttons share one look, with a download icon, in light and dark mode.

title: Tidy-up and speed
changes: Side menu: the stable box uses smaller text and the full width of the menu, so full stable names fit.
Pages draw faster: numbers are formatted far more efficiently, and parts of long pages further down are only laid out when you scroll to them (horse and meeting pages open about a third faster).
Lists sort and page faster: newest-first and biggest-first sorts can use the database's lookups instead of sorting everything; meetings went from about 110 ms to under 10 ms.
New lookups for career earnings, rating and race prize money (built once in a second or so the first time 10.0 starts).
Totals for each list are remembered, so changing the sort or page doesn't count the whole list again.
More of the common pages (Racing, Awards, your horses and your stable's races) are loaded in the background when the viewer starts.
The viewer's own files are only re-sent to the window when they've actually changed.
Clean-up: removed old code and styles left over from earlier versions (the old fold-out family tree, old race cards, the font grid and other unused pieces).

title: Settings uses the same Install an update pop-up
changes: Settings is back to a single “Install an update” button (the extra section from 9.8 is gone).
That button, the link at the bottom of every page and the button on Versions & changes now all open the very same pop-up, so you can choose the file, check it and install from any of them.

title: Install an update is the same in Settings and the pop-up
changes: Settings now has its own “Install an update” section with exactly the same steps and wording as the Install an update window opened from the bottom of the page: your version, what an update does and doesn't touch, choose the file, check what it is, then install.
The window from the bottom of the page and from Versions & changes works the same as before; both now share one set of steps, so they can't drift apart again.

title: Side menu slides over the page on smaller windows
changes: When the window is narrower (about 1150 pixels or less), the ☰ button now slides the side menu in over the top of the page instead of squashing the page into a thin column.
The page underneath stays full width and is dimmed while the menu is open. Click anywhere outside the menu, press Esc, press « or pick a page to close it.
The menu always opens in full (with headings and names) on small windows, even if you've set it to the narrow icon-only style.
On wider windows nothing changes: ☰ still switches between full, icons only and hidden, and your choice is remembered.

title: HRM Viewer is now a desktop app
changes: New HRM Viewer.exe: double-click it and the viewer opens in its own window with its own icon on the taskbar — no browser, no black command window. Closing the window closes the viewer.
It shows a start-up screen while your data opens, keeps to one window (opening it again brings the open window to the front) and keeps its settings separately from the browser.
The first time, it offers to add HRM Viewer to your desktop and Start menu (also in Settings → Desktop app → Add shortcuts).
Drag a database.db onto HRM Viewer.exe to load it.
Installing this update puts HRM Viewer.exe in the viewer's folder. Later versions of the app arrive the same way and are swapped in the next time you open it.
Start.bat and the browser still work exactly as before.

title: Home side menu shows everything
changes: When Home is selected, the side menu starts with You (your profile first) and then lists every area — Racing, Horses, Stables, People, Awards and Settings — with all their pages, so everything is one click from Home.
Home: Rating removed from 'Top earners still alive'.

title: Font dropdowns and save-wide leaders on Home
changes: Settings → Display now starts with two dropdowns: Font (Standard at the top, then every font grouped by kind, each shown in its own typeface, with a search box) and Font colour (Standard, Black, Charcoal, Slate, Navy, Royal blue, Teal, Forest green, Olive, Brown, Burgundy, Plum, Crimson — each shown in its colour, with a lighter version used in dark mode).
Home: the 'Coming up' race cards are gone.

Home: new 'Leaders across the whole save' tables — highest rated horses, most wins (horses), most jockey wins, most trainer wins, top earners of all time, most Group 1 wins, most successful stables and leading sires by progeny earnings.

title: Track records on horse pages
changes: Horse pages have a new Track records panel (below the race record).
Held now: every course record the horse still holds — racecourse and track, distance, time, how much it improved the old record, the race, the jockey and how long it has stood.

Held in the past: records it set that have since been broken — who broke it (or 'itself' if the horse lowered its own record), when and with what time, how long the horse held it, and what the record is now.
Sectional records held: sections of a course and distance where this horse has run the fastest time ever recorded.

title: Reorganised menus
changes: Top menu now has one entry per area: Home · Racing · Horses · Stables · People · Awards, with Settings on the right. Racecourses moved into Racing; Horse table and Pedigrees into Horses; Stable table into Stables.

Side menu follows the area you're in. 'You' is always at the top (your profile, your stables with the dropdown, your horses, your stable's races); below it are the pages for the current area, grouped by what you want to do — e.g. Racing: Results / Coming up / Places; Horses: Horses / Breeding; Awards: Awards / By award; People: jockeys, trainers, head trainers, managers.

Every list page has the same row of tabs for its area (Racing: Meetings · Races · Racecourses; Horses: All horses · Horse table · Pedigrees; Stables: All stables · Stable table; Settings: General · Databases · All tables · Versions & changes).
The page you're on is highlighted in the side menu, even with filters or a later page selected. All charts, tables and pages are unchanged.

title: Dark mode and fonts
changes: Dark mode: Settings → Appearance → Light, Dark, or Match Windows (follows your Windows light/dark setting and switches with it). Every page, table, chart, pop-up and the family tree is styled for it.

Fonts: Settings → Font shows a preview card for every font — 93 free fonts that come with the viewer (Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Montserrat, Poppins, Nunito, IBM Plex, Fira, Merriweather, Playfair Display, JetBrains Mono, Orbitron, Press Start 2P and many more) plus 33 fonts that come with Windows or Office. Search them or filter by kind (clean, narrow, serif, monospaced, display & fun), and click one to use it everywhere.
The bundled fonts work offline. They're all free fonts from Google Fonts; their licences are in fonts-licenses.txt.
Reset settings also puts the theme and font back to standard.

title: Up to 5,000 rows per page
changes: Every long table (Horses, Races, Meetings, Stables, People, Racecourses, Horse table, Stable table, Pedigrees, a stable's Every race, and All tables) now has a 'Rows per page' choice under it: 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1,000, 2,500 or 5,000.
Your choice is remembered for all tables; you can also set it in Settings → Rows per page.

title: Tidier side menu
changes: Racecourses removed from the left side menu (it's still in the top menu).

title: Awards section
changes: New Awards section in the left menu: Awards by year, Hall of Fame and Most awards.

Awards by year shows the winner of every season award for each year side by side: Horse of the Year, Champion Male/Female, the age divisions (2yo, 3yo, 4yo, older), the Asahi Gold distance champions, Sire/Dam/Breeder of the Year, Jockey/Trainer/Head Trainer/Manager/Stablehand of the Year, Stable of the Year, the Thravang Award, the Hall of Fame and the special race-series awards (Triple Crowns etc.). Pick one group from the list to see just that.
Each winner shows their stable and the award's value; hover for the full description and the runners-up. Your own wins are highlighted.
Most awards ranks every horse, person and stable by awards won, with which awards and in which years.
Group 1, 2, 3 and Listed race wins are not part of the Awards section.
Databases and All tables are no longer in the left menu (they're under Settings).

title: Settings holds All tables and Databases; side menu can shrink
changes: All tables is no longer in the top menu. Settings now has tabs for General, Databases, All tables and Versions & changes.
Fixed the small scroll arrows that could appear at the right of the top menu.

Side menu: the ☰ button at the left of the top menu switches between the full menu, just icons, and hidden; « at the top of the side menu shrinks or expands it. Your choice is remembered (also in Settings → Side menu).
Fixed tables showing several CSV buttons (e.g. Track records on racecourse pages): every table now has exactly one.

title: CSV everywhere and choose the watched file
changes: Horse table: the Speed, Stamina, Acceleration and Strength columns are removed (they're still on each horse's page).

Every table in the app now has a '⤓ CSV' button that downloads it as a spreadsheet file, including tables on horse, race, meeting, stable, person, racecourse and pedigree pages. Hidden rows (e.g. older awards) are included.

List pages (Horses, Races, Meetings, Stables, People, Racecourses) and every table under All tables now have an Export CSV button that downloads every matching row, not just the page you're on, with your filters and sort.

Settings → Automatic updates: you can now type or paste a different file to watch ('Watch this file'). It has to be the same save as the open database; if it's newer than the stored data it's loaded straight away.

title: Automatic updates from your save
changes: New in Settings → Automatic updates: turn it on and the viewer watches the database.db the open database was loaded from. Every time the game saves, it waits until the file is finished and loads it the normal way (newest records win, history is kept).
It only loads the same career automatically, never an older file or a different save; those are left for you to choose with Load database.
Choose how long to wait after the file changes (15 seconds to 5 minutes) and the shortest gap between updates (1 minute to 1 hour). 'Check now' looks straight away.
A '● Auto' marker at the top shows it's on (amber while a change is waiting, spinning while it loads). When new data arrives the game date updates and a banner offers to show the new data.
Works per database: each database watches the file it was loaded from.

title: More chart time ranges
changes: Settings → Charts open showing now offers All, the last 10, 5, 3, 2 or 1 years, or the last 9, 6, 3 or 1 months.
Every chart has the same choices as short buttons (ALL, 10Y, 5Y… 1M). Only ranges shorter than the chart's history are shown, and hovering a button says what it shows.

title: Settings tab and tidier positions
changes: Finishing positions now sit on one line everywhere (race record, results, meetings): a badge for the place (gold, silver, bronze or grey) followed by 'of 16'.

New Settings tab (top right, and in the left menu) with all the viewer's own settings in one place: text size, hover cards on/off, pedigree gender colours, which time range charts open on, your main stable, the open database, version and updates, and Reset settings.
The text size buttons moved from the menu bar to Settings; the hover cards switch moved from the bottom of the page to Settings.

title: Top speed in sectionals
changes: Sectionals (race pages and meeting results): new Top speed column for every runner — the fastest average speed it held over any one section, and which section that was. The fastest in the race is shown in purple, and you can sort by it.
Fastest sections now includes a Top speed box with the horse that ran fastest in the race.

title: Pop-ups and better charts
changes: Horse page race record: new Trainer, Stable and Gear columns.
Gear is shown as short letters (B, E, T…); hover to see the full names (Blinkers, Earplugs, Tongue tie). This is used in the race record and the form guides too.

Hover cards: hover over any horse, person, stable, race or racecourse link for a quick summary (record, earnings, rating, form, sire and dam; rides and wins; horses and prize money; top three in a race…). They can be turned off at the bottom of the page.
Tooltips across the app are now quicker and easier to read (grades, finishing positions, gear, ability bars and more).
Charts: hover anywhere for the exact date and every line's value; click a name in the legend to hide or show that line; pick a time range (All, 3 years, 1 year, 6 months) on longer charts.
Finishing positions chart: the hover shows the race, course, distance and field, and clicking a dot opens that race.

title: All your stables
changes: The viewer now finds every stable you own (including stables owned by your stables) and every stable you hold shares in, directly or through one of your stables.
Left menu: 'Your stables' has a dropdown to pick which of them to open; 'Your horses' follows your choice.

On the page of any of your stables (and its Every race page) there's a bar to scroll through them: ◀ and ▶ go to the previous and next, the dropdown jumps straight to one, and 'See all' lists them with your role, shares, horses, starts, wins, prize money and net worth.
The viewer remembers the last stable you picked, separately for each database.

title: Several databases
changes: Keep several databases side by side, e.g. different saves or careers, and switch between them. The name of the open database is shown at the top right; click it, or Databases in the left menu.
Databases page: see every database with its player, game date, size and when it was last loaded; open, rename or delete them.
Move your existing stored data into the new structure with one click. It is moved, not copied, so it's instant and nothing in it changes. Until then it keeps working as 'Stored data (old layout)'.
Bring in the stored data from another HRM Viewer folder (for example an older copy you unzipped somewhere else) as its own database, copied or moved. A game database.db works there too.
Load database: choose to load into the open database or into a new database with its own name.
If you load a file from a different save, the viewer now offers to keep both by loading it as a separate database.
Each database gets the newest stats tables the first time it's opened (about 15 seconds).

title: Form by distance and pedigree highlights
changes: Horse page Form guide: new By distance group showing starts and wins-seconds-thirds at each distance the horse has run (to the nearest 100 m), with win % and place %. The next start's distance is highlighted.

Pedigree page, Most influential ancestors: new Show tick box on each horse. Ticked horses are highlighted in their own colour everywhere they appear in the family tree, with a count per generation of how many highlighted horses are in it. A Clear highlights button removes them all.
Family tree (8, 12, 16 generations): every generation has a ▾/▸ button to hide or expand it, plus Expand all and Hide all.

Family tree (4 generations): show or hide each generation (parents, grandparents, great-grandparents, 3× great-grandparents), plus Expand all and Hide all. The chart shrinks when the outer generations are hidden.

title: Sectionals on meeting results
changes: Meeting results pages (Races tab → Meetings → a meeting) now show sectionals under every race result, for all runners. Click the Sectionals heading to fold a race's sectionals away.

New Fastest sections boxes on race pages and meeting results. For each section (1st, 2nd and 3rd quarter, 75–90%, final 10%) and the last 50%, they show the fastest time, the horse, its average speed and where it finished.

title: Track condition and sectionals
changes: Race and meeting pages: Betting handle replaced by Track condition (e.g. Good 4, Soft 6, Heavy 9 on turf; Fast / Good / Muddy / Sloppy on dirt; Synthetic). The save has no going rating, so it is worked out from the race-day weather and rain amount, shown under it.

Race pages: new Sectionals table for every runner. It shows the time for each section of the race (1st, 2nd and 3rd quarters, 75–90% and the final 10%), with position, distance behind the leader and average speed at each point, plus finish time, last-half time and speed at the finish. The fastest section in the race is shown in purple.

Racecourse pages: new Sectional records table. For each distance and track it shows the fastest time ever run for each section, the horse that ran it and the race date, plus how many runs have been timed.
The save only keeps sectional data for races from about August 2018 onwards, so older races have no sectionals. Sectionals are kept when you load newer saves.

title: Family tree list view and sortable tables
changes: Family tree opens at 4 generations again, with the usual chart.

8, 12 and 16 generations now show a list with one row per generation: how many ancestors are recorded out of how many possible, then every ancestor with its position (D = dam, S = sire, so DS = dam's sire), † if deceased, name and year foaled.
Gender colours (orange for dams, teal for sires) can be turned off. Click any name to move the tree to that horse.
Generations 1 to 9 show straight away; for larger ones click Show (they can hold thousands of horses).

Copy all copies the whole list as text. Copy for spreadsheet copies one row per ancestor (generation, position, sex, name, born, died, record, earnings, horse ID) ready to paste into Excel or Google Sheets.

Every table in the app can now be sorted: click a column heading, click again to reverse. Numbers, money, dates and times sort properly, form panels stay with their runner, and 'show latest' lists keep showing the top few after sorting.

title: One text size for the whole app
changes: The A− / A+ control (now called Text size) changes all text in the app, not just tables: menus, headings, panels, tiles, charts and form panels all scale together.
Every page now uses the same type scale (body text, small notes and labels, headings), so fonts match across tabs.
Text can now go smaller, down to 8px (it was 10px). The control itself stays a readable size.
Horse page Form guide: jockey and trainer details are removed, and the text is a step smaller. Race-page form panels still show jockey and trainer stats.

title: Horse page rework
changes: Offspring tables now have an Age column (or the age a foal died at). This is on the horse page and on the pedigree page's brother/sister and half-sibling tables.

New Form guide above the race record. It has the same details as the race-page form panel: details grid, win/place ring, short form, and jockey and trainer stats. If the horse has an upcoming race, conditions for that race are highlighted; otherwise it shows a whole-career summary.
Abilities, Mind & health, Distance preference and Running style moved below the race record.
Abilities no longer show the potential numbers. Each ability is marked Peak reached, Past peak, Below its best or Still improving, with a count of how many have peaked.
Traits and Health history now sit side by side.
Awards now include G2, G3 and Listed wins as well as G1. Race awards link to the race, and the panel heading counts each grade.
Awards and News show the latest 5, with a Show all button to expand.
Charts now mark each year with a labelled line (and months in between), and show the first and last dates with their year.

New Finishing positions chart: one line of where the horse finished in each start (1st at the top), with gold, silver and bronze dots for wins and places and a dashed field-size line. Hover a dot to see the race.

title: Form guide on race pages
changes: Each runner's line now shows barrier, age, colour and sex, jockey (J:), trainer (T:), stable, last-5 form, career record and win/place %, plus last start for upcoming races or time, margin and SP for results.

Click the arrow on a runner for a form panel: details (sire, dam, dam's sire, trainer, prize money, settling position, gear, days since last start), a win/place ring, short form (track, distance, track and distance, 1st–4th up, season, weather, surface, direction, jockey on the horse) with today's conditions highlighted, jockey and trainer stats, and last starts (place, track, distance, class, barrier, jockey, condition, time, average speed, margin, SP, days, prize, first three home).
"Open all form" opens every runner at once. The same runner lines and panels are on meeting pages.
All form figures are as they stood before that race.
Pages can be wider so the extra columns fit.

title: Meetings, stable race history, compact pedigree charts
changes: Races tab now has two sub-tabs: Meetings (each meeting as a summary row: date, meeting, course, races, top race, prize money, weather) and Races (the list as before).
Click a meeting to see every race at it, with full results or the field, plus links to the previous and next meeting at that course.
Every stable has an "Every race" page: all of its runs ever, filterable by result, race type and year, sortable, with Export CSV.
Family trees at 8, 12 and 16 generations now use the same chart as 4 generations, drawn smaller, with the most repeated ancestors coloured and Sire's side / Dam's side buttons.
Home: the Next up strip is gone; your recent and upcoming rides are at the top.
Race type badges (G1, G2, G3, Listed…) are smaller everywhere.

title: New look and deeper pedigrees
changes: New look in the style of a racing/betting site: dark navy header, white menu bar with icons, left sidebar of quick links, white cards on a light grey page.
Home: a "Next up" strip of the next races and race cards for your next rides (or the next Group races), with the field and ratings.
Odds and ratings shown in number boxes on race pages.
Family trees: choose 4, 8, 12 or 16 generations. Your choice is remembered.

8–16 generations: a fold-out family tree, the most influential ancestors (how often each appears and their share of the pedigree), generation-by-generation completeness, and the straight sire and dam lines.
Inbreeding coefficient (COI) for the chosen number of generations.

title: Versions page
changes: New Versions page listing every version and what changed in it (link at the bottom of every page).
"Go back to version …" moved here from the bottom of the page, and you can now go back to any of the saved earlier versions, not just the last one.

title: Speed
changes: Pages you've opened before now open instantly until you load a new save.
After starting, or after loading a save, the viewer warms up in the background so first clicks are quick too.
Database connections are kept open between clicks, making everything about twice as fast.
Loading a save is about 25% faster (career and stable stats are worked out in half the time).

title: In-app updates
changes: "Install an update" at the bottom of every page installs update files without unzipping anything.
The current version is backed up before each update, and you can go back to it.
If a new version fails to start, the previous one is put back automatically.
Updates can never touch your stored data.

title: Correct past winners
changes: Fixed: a race's past runnings mixed in different races that share its name at other courses (e.g. the two January Cups). Races are now matched by the game's own race id.
"Past winners" now shows jockey, stable, distance, time and prize, like the game; scheduled future runnings are listed separately.
Times are shown to the thousandth exactly as the game shows them.
Search lists same-named races separately, each with its course.

title: Table text size
changes: Table text size control (A− / A+ / Reset) in the tab bar; applies to every table and is remembered.
Tables are slightly smaller by default.

title: Top race fix
changes: Fixed: racecourse meetings showed the wrong top race (G3 above G1) and ignored Listed races. Now ranked G1, G2, G3, Listed, with the race name.

title: Track records
changes: Track records on every racecourse page: the fastest winning time at each distance on each track.
Click a distance to see every earlier record holder, when they set it and by how much.

title: Stable records
changes: All-time starts, wins, 2nds, 3rds, G1/G2/G3/Listed wins and total stakes won on the Stables tab and each stable's page.
The same figures added to the Stable table.

title: Loads build on your data
changes: Loading a newer save updates the stored data: newer records win, and history the game deletes is kept.
Asks first if a file is from a different career or older than what's stored; an older file can add just its missing records.
Horses, people and stables the game removes are kept and marked "Removed from game".
Load history on the Home page; "Start fresh" option when loading.

title: Pedigrees and stats tables
changes: Pedigrees tab: sires, dams and broodmare sires ranked by their foals' results, plus a four-generation family tree with siblings.
Horse table and Stable table tabs: every horse and stable with key stats, sortable, with Export CSV.

title: First version
changes: Home, Horses, Races, Stables, People and Racecourses pages, all linked together, plus search.
All tables: every table in the save, with sorting and filters.
Load new database from a file path or by choosing the file.
